title: Connection hub
blurb: Multi-tab SharedWorker presence hub recording the real connect event e.data and typeof for every client across both the run-a-worker and existing-worker constructor paths.
question: Do multi-tab and multi-connection SharedWorker handshakes across both HTML spec algorithms deliver consistent connect event metadata to a shared presence roster?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153, two pages plus an extra connection produced a 3-row roster (1 run-a-worker, 2 constructor) all reporting e.data === null, and leaving in tab 2 cooperatively updated the roster. Chrome 160 empty-string branch not verified.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 (legacy null branch verified); not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: SharedWorker ports have no worker-side close event to detect tab disconnects automatically
friction.repro: Close or navigate away from a connected tab without sending an explicit disconnect message; the SharedWorker keeps the stale MessagePort in its client list.
friction.browser: Chrome for Testing 153 (and current SharedWorker implementations)
friction.workaround: Send a cooperative leave/bye message over the port (for example on pagehide or explicit Leave) and prune dead clients via heartbeat or cooperative teardown.
